title: Tiny Stack, Big Tree
intro: Loops are offline and your call stack holds only [b]30[/b] frames. Somewhere in this tree of corridors is the exit. Explore smart: a call that goes one tile deeper must also bring you back.
cs_note: [b]Tree recursion[/b] keeps only the current branch on the stack, so its depth is the height of the tree, not the length of the walk. A recursive wall follower (tail recursion) adds a frame for every step and overflows.
hints: Let A(): if there's a path ahead, step in, explore every direction from there, then step back out.
B can be the step back: turn around, move, turn around.

After stepping in, A explores ahead, turns left and explores, turns right twice and explores, then turns left to face forward again, and B steps back out. Every call ends where it started, facing the same way. With no path ahead, A does nothing: that's the base case. The run ends the moment the robot reaches the exit.
